Schedule deep-dive on SOC2/HSM integration with Samir

summary: Redwood AE + SE walked Aster through data lifecycle and console toggles: how to disable request storage, enable PII masking, retention windows, and how Optimize recommends batching vs caching given privacy constraints. Customer asked about KMS/HSM, audit logs, and an on-prem hybrid mode. Agreed next steps: sandbox, sample schema, POC run dates.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-08-21 16:00 PDT | Duration: 47m | Attendees: Liam Carter (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Dr. Elena Morales (Aster), Samir Rao (Aster Security Lead), Jae Park (Aster Platform)

[00:00] Liam (Redwood): okay hi everyone thanks for joining, quick intro I'm Liam Carter, AE on the account, Maya here is our solutions engineer.
[00:08] Maya (Redwood): hey all, nice to meet you, we'll do a short walkthrough of the Console and then jump into a quick API example for request storage and PII masking.
[00:15] Elena (Aster): great, high level we care about not persisting PHI, retention windows, and an auditable trail. We run in multi-tenant clusters and need to show compliance for our hospital partners.
[00:28] Samir (Aster): and encryption — we require KMS with customer-managed keys, ideally HSM backed, plus SSO and RBAC integration.
[00:36] Maya: totally, we'll show the private deployment controls but also the hosted API toggles — the Console exposes a per-route storage toggle and a masking profile, also Audit Trails that can redact values on export.
[00:49] Liam: quick note, we'll demonstrate the toggle named "store_requests" in the Console and then show the API headers you can use for per-request overrides.
[00:58] Jae (Aster): per-request overrides are important for our ingestion pipeline, sometimes dev logs are okay to keep but not production PII.
[01:10] Maya: right, so first screen — Console > Project > Data Controls. You can set default behavior: store_requests = on/off, retention_days = 7/30/90/365, pii_masking_profile = strict/medical-lite/custom.
[01:26] Elena: can you show the custom profile? we have custom PHI fields like mrn and chart_id that standard profiles don't catch.
[01:34] Maya: sure — opens custom mask editor. It's a simple regex-and-rule builder; you can list fields, supply regex, and choose redaction style (remove, mask, hash). It also supports lookups so if you want a hash stable across requests we can salt it with KMS.
[01:52] Samir: wait you said KMS — where does that live in the flow?
[01:56] Maya: Good Q. For hosted, you can bring your key via customer-managed KMS; the service wraps KMS calls in HSM-backed envelopes. For Private, we support HSM connectors and your on-prem key store. On-screen I'll show the key-binding workflow — it's under Security > Key Management.
[02:12] Liam: also worth calling out audit logs — every change to a masking profile and every retention toggle flip is recorded with actor and timestamp. Exports can be restricted and the raw exports themselves can be redacted so the audit archive doesn't leak PII.
[02:26] Elena: how granular is the audit? per-request or only control plane changes?
[02:31] Maya: both — control plane changes get full actor metadata, request-level logs can be set to record only metadata (no prompt/response) or record redacted prompt/response depending on store_requests and pii policy.
[02:44] Jae: show the API example for setting the per-request header please.
[02:48] Maya: yep — copy/paste from the Console snippet: POST /v1/generate with header X-Redwood-Store-Request: false and X-Redwood-PII-Profile: custom-med. In the SDK it's a request option. Note: setting store_requests=false means tokens will not be persisted to request storage; ephemeral caching may still use K-V cache in memory during inference unless you opt that out.
[03:09] Samir: what's that KV cache you mentioned — could it be leaked to logs?
[03:12] Maya: The KV cache is in-memory and per-inference session; it's not written to disk by default. You can enable ephemeral_kv_persistence for debugging but we recommend keeping it off for PHI workloads.
[03:24] Liam: another piece is Optimize — we can still recommend batching and caching strategies that respect your store settings. For example, prefix caching on non-PII request classes will reduce cost without persisting PII. Maya will show an example optimize suggestion.
[03:38] Maya: switching to the Optimize tab — it analyzes token patterns and suggests turning on short-term prefix cache for sessions labelled "consent=true" while forcing store_requests=false for consent=false. You can bind labels from your app and the routing rules enforce policy.
[03:55] Elena: that label binding — is it enforced by policy or just advisory?
[03:59] Maya: enforced, we have a policy engine. If route label consent=false then the runtime rejects enabling caching that would persist any portion of the prompt/response.
[04:09] Jae: walkthrough on retention windows — what happens when retention_days hits zero?
[04:14] Maya: once retention_days expires the system runs an irreversible purge flow. For hosted there's a 24-hour purge job that deletes request artifacts and rotates related indexes. For private, you can schedule a run or trigger immediate purge via API. We also provide purge receipts in audit.
[04:30] Samir: purge receipts sound good — must be tamper-evident?
[04:33] Liam: receipts include hash signatures signed by our service keys and can be validated by your key; for Private we can sign with your key.
[04:41] Elena: can we do a live sample — create a custom profile and run a request then show it not present in storage?
[04:47] Maya: yeah quick demo — creating profile 'aster-mrn' regex: [A-Z0-9]{8}
[04:55] [04:55] Maya (typing): created. Now toggle store_requests to false on route /nlp/infer-aster.
[05:02] [05:02] Maya: run sample request...
[05:07] [05:07] Sample request (Maya): {"input":"Patient MRN AB12345678 reports severe chest pain"}
[05:12] [05:12] System: request accepted — store_requests=false — response streamed
[05:20] Maya: now checking request storage explorer— nothing in the persistent bucket for that request id — only a minimal metadata row (timestamp, route, status) because store_requests was false.
[05:34] Jae: how about logs and debug traces? they sometimes capture full spans.
[05:39] Maya: debug traces are gated by a separate flag 'debug_traces=true' — if disabled traces capture only trace ids and latency. If enabled for a session we always keep it ephemeral and require a manual retention approval.
[05:53] Samir: can we integrate our SIEM for alerts on retention flips?
[05:57] Liam: yes webhooks + syslog integration on control plane events. We can push change events to your SIEM.
[06:04] Elena: one question on legal discovery — if a hospital partner requests records, how do you provide evidence without exposing PHI?
[06:11] Maya: we provide redacted exports and purge receipts. If you need original content for legal reason, you can create a sealed request export that requires dual approval and exports to your secured S3 with encryption. That's a manual audited flow.
[06:25] Liam: quick pause — anyone want to jump in with concerns?
[06:29] Samir: how do you handle model evals and logging for quality monitoring? we can't surface PHI to human reviewers.
[06:36] Maya: we have an eval pipeline that supports synthetic prompt substitutions: token-level pseudonymization and automated QA metrics. You can route sample sets through a masking pass before it ever hits human reviewers.
[06:48] Jae: okay that helps. Another ops question — we run on GCE and AWS, how does private mode work with our VPC?
[06:55] Maya: Private connects via VPC peering or private link, and the control plane can be hosted or air-gapped. For on-prem you run the edge package and bind to your KMS. Network egress can be locked.
[07:07] Elena: any limits on per-request header overrides? we might need a lambda to flip store_requests on some flows.
[07:13] Liam: you can override per request up to the route policy limits; we also support ephemeral tokens from a short-lived auth role for programmatic flips. It's rate-limited for audit reasons.
[07:24] [07:24] Maya (Redwood): demo snippet of SDK usage: redwood.generate({route: 'nlp/infer-aster', storeRequests:false, piiProfile:'aster-mrn'}) — shows that it attaches headers and logs minimal metadata.
[07:40] Elena: curious about retention_day granularity — hourly? daily?
[07:44] Maya: retention is daily granularity for hosted, you can request hourly in Private for stricter SLAs.
[07:52] Samir: what about backups and snapshots? our infra policy requires nightly backups, but they can't contain PHI.
[07:59] Maya: backups are policy-aware; if store_requests=false then backups do not contain request payloads. Snapshots of config are fine. For extra assurance we can run a backup scrub job that verifies no PII fields per your schema.
[08:12] Jae: demo the audit export — show a sanitized CSV.
[08:16] [08:16] Maya (typing): exporting audit, selecting 'sanitize on export' — preview shows actor/timestamp/action but request_id field hashed.
[08:26] Elena: does hashing use customer salt?
[08:29] Maya: yes you can use your KMS key to salt/hmac the ids so only you can resolve them.
[08:36] Liam: let's surface a typical customer flow: data arrives -> route label applied (consent true/false) -> runtime policy decides caching/retention -> if consent=false, store_requests off, mask profile applied -> metrics still emitted for billing but token payloads omitted.
[08:57] Samir: metrics for billing — do they include token counts? we need to show costs without leaking content.
[09:02] Maya: token counts are integer metrics only; we don't include token text. We also break down per-route latencies and cost attribution.
[09:12] Elena: show how Optimize recommends quantization if we want lower cost but still keep PHI private.
[09:18] Maya: Optimize suggests model variants with quantization that run faster but doesn't change data handling. The recommendation includes expected latency, throughput, and whether the model variant supports deterministic masking hooks.
[09:30] [09:30] Liam: interruption — small typo in the console, bear with me...
[09:34] Jae: ha, live product demo fun.
[09:36] Maya: wrapping up with an API example for purge: POST /v1/purge with body {route:'nlp/infer-aster', before: '2025-08-01T00:00:00Z'} and you'd get a purge receipt id.
[09:49] Elena: after purge can we run an integrity check to ensure nothing remains?
[09:53] Maya: yes we provide a verification API that returns the purge status and hash signatures.
[09:58] Samir: what are the SLA guarantees for purge windows?
[10:02] Liam: for hosted, we claim 24-48 hours for irreversible delete; for Dedicated we can contract lower windows and Private is based on your schedule.
[10:13] Elena: two operational asks — we need an example retention policy JSON for our compliance team and a sample export showing pseudonymization flow.
[10:21] Liam: noted, we'll send both.
[10:24] Maya: quick Q from my side: can you share a sample of your log schema and a list of fields you consider PHI? that will let us pre-build the mask profile.
[10:33] Samir: yes we'll send it to you, Samir@aster.corp.
[10:37] [10:37] Liam: OK last section — security/compliance notes. We support SAML SSO, RBAC with role-level segregation for audit access, and the control plane supports IP allow lists.
[10:49] Elena: about human reviewers — we need a review queue that only gets pseudonymized content.
[10:54] Maya: that's the default for evals: all human-review queues receive substituted tokens; you can set an allowlist for emergency unmasking with dual approval.
[11:05] Jae: can we have a test account now? we'd like to kick the POC next week.
[11:09] Liam: yes we'll provision a sandbox with the aster-mrn mask profile and example route. Expect an invite today.
[11:15] Elena: timeline — we want POC results in 2 weeks to present to the compliance board.
[11:20] Liam: sounds reasonable. We'll target POC run window 2025-09-02 to 2025-09-10.
[11:28] Maya: final callouts — remember to include your sample log schema and identify emergency unmask approvers.
[11:34] Samir: will do.
[11:38] Liam: recap and next steps: we'll send retention policy JSON, provision sandbox creds, and Maya will run the retention toggle test with your sample load. Any last q's?
[11:49] Elena: none. Thanks everyone.
[11:52] Liam: thanks, meeting end.

Notes: transcription shows occasional duplicated timestamps and small transcription artifacts (e.g., "KV" as "K-V"), speaker interruptions preserved.
